title: Edge telemetry buffer refactor and protocol shim to reduce allocation churn
creator: Maya Chen
description: Refactor the in-service 'edge' telemetry buffer and introduce a lightweight protocol shim to reduce per-request allocations, decrease CPU overhead in the telemetry hot path, and improve tail latencies for small requests. Current behaviour serializes spans/metrics/logs synchronously into transient byte arrays and uses multiple goroutine handoffs; this produces allocation churn and GC pressure under high concurrency (seen in p99 CPU and latency spikes in Dedicated customers during load tests).
background: Over the past year we've accumulated quick fixes around the telemetry forwarder: per-request JSON and proto allocations, ephemeral buffers per span, and synchronous HTTP/GRPC exporter calls. Several runtime incidents (see postmortem links) indicate spike in GC pauses correlated with telemetry bursts. Earlier tickets addressed sampling and exporter selection, but this ticket targets runtime allocation patterns inside the edge buffer and the serialization path.
goals: Reduce telemetry-related heap allocs by >= 60% in the runtime hot path
Lower telemetry-driven p99 latency contribution by at least 25ms under representative load
Make telemetry encode/export nonblocking for request-critical threads by introducing bounded ring buffer + background worker pool
Introduce a small, stable protocol shim so future exporter upgrades (OTLP/gRPC->HTTP/JSON/UDP) only need to implement the shim contract
Keep feature parity (sampling, attributes, trace ids) and preserve existing audit links for Private deployments
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark: synthetic trace workload with 5000 rps and 20 spans/request shows >=60% alloc reduction compared to baseline
E2E: Dedicated cluster soak (24h) with production sampling and traffic shows no regression in request latency and improved telemetry CPU share
New protocol shim documented with interface spec and example exporter (HTTP/OTLP) in repo
All new code covered by unit tests, and benchmark harness checked into telemetry/perf/benchmarks
Rollout plan documented and feature-flagged; can be toggled off on global control plane within 5 minutes
design_notes: We will replace per-span transient buffers with a pool of preallocated byte slices (size classes based on 256/1k/4k). Introduce a lock-free single-producer-multiple-consumer ring for each runtime worker to batch serialization; use a small background worker pool to perform encoding and network export. The protocol shim will define a compact binary envelope (versioned) with minimal headers: type, length, timestamp, tenant-id, checksum. Initial shim encoders: OTLP HTTP exporter and a passthrough gRPC exporter for backward compatibility.
tradeoffs: Using a custom binary shim reduces immediate CPU overhead but adds one more translation layer and maintenance surface. We avoid changing the user's observable data model, but decoding human-readable traces will require tooling. Pooling reduces allocations but needs careful sizing to avoid OOM on sustained spikes—we choose bounded pools and circuit-breaker on exporter failures.
progress_updates: 2025-07-08: Spike analysis complete; identified allocation sites via pprof (telemetry/encoder.go and forwarder/queue.go). Added initial microbench harness.
2025-07-16: Prototype ring buffer and pooled-slice allocator implemented (branch: telemetry/edge-refactor). Unit benchmarks show ~48% alloc reduction for small spans.
2025-07-24: Integrated background worker pool and OTLP-HTTP shim encoder. End-to-end tests passing in local cluster. Observed CPU drop in synthetic load by ~22%.

2025-08-01: PRs opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3142 (ring-buffer & pools), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3158 (protocol shim + OTLP HTTP encoder). Requesting design review from @Lena Kovacs and @Diego Ramos.

2025-08-05: Bench harness added to CI perf job and 24h soak plan scheduled for Dedicated staging cluster (staging-dedicated-7). Initial soak shows stable memory and improved tail latency; collecting more data before canary.

implementation_steps: Finalize interface spec for protocol shim (telemetry/shim/README.md)
Merge pooled allocator and ring buffer implementation behind feature flag 'edge_telemetry_v2'
Add background worker pool with bounded queue, implement exporter circuit-breaker
Create OTLP-HTTP encoder and small example gRPC passthrough exporter
Add benchmarks and CI gating; run perf job against staging Dedicated cluster
Canary rollout: 1% hosts -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring alerts
Post-rollout: remove legacy serialization if no issues for 4 weeks
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Bounded pools may be exhausted during sudden bursts leading to dropped telemetry. Mitigation: metrics + alerts for pool saturation and fallback to synchronous path with backoff.
Risk: Protocol shim bugs could corrupt telemetry for older debug tools. Mitigation: versioned envelope and compatibility mode; keep legacy exporter behind flag.
Risk: Hidden CPU regression in exporter path. Mitigation: run exporter-only microbench and compare across hardware profiles (A100, T4, CPU-only).
qa_plan: Unit tests: allocator correctness, ring buffer concurrency, exporter circuit-breaker
Perf tests: benchmark harness with parameterized span sizes and service counts
Soak tests: 24h Dedicated staging soak with production sampling and tenant mix
Regression tests: verify no lost spans for high-sampling customers during canary
Observability: add dashboards for telemetry_pool_usage, telemetry_queue_latency, telemetry_export_errors
rollback_plan: Feature flag controlled. If canary shows regressions we will revert to legacy serializer path by toggling 'edge_telemetry_v2' to false and draining background workers. For partial failures we can disable exporters at region level via control plane policy to prevent tenant-wide impact.
notes: This ticket consolidates several past ad-hoc fixes into a deterministic and bounded architecture for telemetry in the runtime. The aim is not to remove telemetry but to make it predictable and cheap. Keep an eye on Private deployment packaging implications (build tags for HSM/KMS integrations) and confirm packaging tests for on-prem images.
